def: A Claude Code plugin that turns a learning goal into a verified, interactive documentation site in four stages: insight, brief, research and compose.
What the compose stage builds for a topic: index.html, one page per module and the assets, written from the dossier by page writers and readable offline.
One learning goal and everything atlaspedia keeps for it under topics/<slug>/. The slug is the topic's short code name, at most 24 characters, such as map-projections.
The refined statement of what you want to learn and why, with the policies derived from it (depth, source types, verification level). Written after the interview and confirmed by you.
The field scout's quick map of a topic's subfields and key sources, made in the background during the interview.
The short, committed file for catching up on a topic: what you want, the stage reached, one row per module and stage, what runs next and the caveats.
A topic's name, description, tags, status and dates: everything the root dictionary knows about it.
The self-contained index.html at the repository root that lists every topic, generated by build_index.py from the topic cards.
The research brief: audience, scope, modules, depth and source policy. Reviewed by an agent that never saw the interview, then approved by you.
The verified research for a topic: one file per module plus 00-overview.md. The only source of facts the page writers may use.
The consolidator's file: running-example parameter sheet, overlaps, glossary and bibliography seeds, media list, conflicts and the build notes that become page specs.
The one concrete case a topic returns to on every page, such as one world map of country areas, so numbers stay consistent across modules.
A Python script that checks what an agent wrote and ends with a RESULT line; a plan row is ticked only after its gate passes.
The single machine-readable line, RESULT: followed by key=value pairs, that ends every agent report and every script run.
A line an agent adds to its report when its instructions made the job harder; the main agent turns it into a lesson for the workflow.
A fact a page needs but the dossier does not have. The writer marks it, and the main agent sends a researcher to fill it; a writer never guesses.
The compose stage's page table and writer assignments; scaffold.py turns it into the site registry.
How a topic is built: site (one page per module, full navigation) or single (one self-contained page of about 250 KB at most). Chosen by the refiner or forced with --site or --single.
assets/site.json and the generated assets/site.js: every page in reading order. The runtime builds navigation, search, the pager and the overview widgets from it.
A page with a level in the registry. Modules show a mark-complete button and count towards the progress bar; synthesis and reference pages do not.
The markup page writers may use, in skills/compose/components/: one folder per module with a README and copy-ready snippets.
The last section of every page except the overview and the glossary: verified sources, review date, demo count and open gaps, computed from the page itself.
How much a map projection stretches distances at a point, the ratio of a tiny length on the map to the same length on the globe; 1 where the projection is true to scale.
